main.description: Begin a device-pairing flow (OAuth 2.0 device-authorization style). Returns a `deviceId` plus a short human-typable `userCode` and the `verificationUri` where a signed-in user approves the pairing. The caller then polls `dev.cocore.devicePair.poll` until approval. The optional input lets an application (rather than a provider machine) say who it is: `appName` is shown on the approve screen, `keyName` names the minted API key so the user can recognise and revoke it, and `returnUrl` is where the approve screen sends the browser afterwards. `returnUrl` is honoured only for hosts the deployment allowlists; anything else is dropped silently, never rejected.

appDid.description: The requesting application's DID. When present the AppView reads the app's `dev.cocore.app.registration` record: the approve screen shows that record's `name` (the `appName` field is ignored) and `returnUrl` is honoured only if it matches one of the record's `returnUrls` AND the return host proves ownership via `/.well-known/cocore-app.json`. A DID with no registration record is rejected with InvalidRequest (AppNotRegistered).

appName.description: Human name of the requesting application, shown on the approve screen.

keyName.description: Name for the API key minted on approval.

returnUrl.description: Where to send the browser after approval. Must be https and on an allowlisted host.

userCode.description: Short code the user types at the verification URI.

expiresInSecs.description: Seconds until this pairing attempt expires.

errors.name: RateLimited
errors.description: Too many pairing attempts from this client; retry later.

errors.name: InvalidRequest
errors.description: `appDid` is not a DID, or has no `dev.cocore.app.registration` record (message begins `AppNotRegistered`).
